profilePeriod: 2015–2016 presidential campaign, informed by her 2009–2013 diplomatic record; earlier positions dated explicitly and later public remarks checked through September 2026.

sources.title: Campaign voting-rights proposal
sources.evidence: Automatic voter registration, restored Voting Rights Act, national early-voting minimum, voting rights restored after sentences.

sources.title: Campaign criminal-justice proposal
sources.evidence: National police use-of-force guidelines and oversight, local police retained, mandatory-minimum reform, treatment instead of incarceration for minor drug offenses, states as marijuana laboratories, end private prisons.

sources.title: Campaign immigration proposal
sources.evidence: Citizenship pathway, DACA/DAPA, humane targeted enforcement and border protection, end family/private detention, English and citizenship education alongside integration.

sources.title: Campaign national-security proposal
sources.evidence: Supports NATO, Israel defense, sanctions against Iran and Russia, Iran nuclear agreement, Cuba engagement and lifting embargo, New START, diplomacy and military counterterrorism.

sources.title: Campaign health-care proposal
sources.evidence: ACA and public option, Medicare buy-in from 55, Medicaid expansion incentives, community health centers, competition and drug-price penalties; legal abortion.

sources.title: Campaign Wall Street reform
sources.evidence: Risk fee for large banks, stronger Volcker rule, authority to break risky financial firms apart, tax on harmful high-frequency trading, prosecution of fraud.

sources.title: Campaign manufacturing proposal
sources.evidence: Buy American, manufacturing partnerships and tax incentives, reject TPP in its concluded form, enforce trade rules against Chinese steel practices, penalize offshoring; still compete in global markets.

sources.title: TIME: Clinton explains Christianity and politics
sources.evidence: Identifies as Methodist Christian; religious obligations of charity, care for prisoners and strangers guide politics; rejects harsh religious condemnation.

sources.title: Campaign LGBT equality
sources.evidence: Supports same-sex marriage and adoption equality, Equality Act, gender-identity protections, transgender military service, end conversion therapy for minors.

sources.title: Campaign technology and innovation
sources.evidence: STEM, broadband, research, startups and technology exports; net neutrality, privacy safeguards and competition.

sources.title: Campaign climate proposal
sources.evidence: Renewables and efficiency, cut oil consumption and energy waste, preserve public lands, sensitive areas off limits to production; clean industrial growth rather than deindustrialization.

sources.title: ACS C&EN: candidates answer ScienceDebate
sources.evidence: Candidate responses endorse research partnerships and advanced space program; scientific research and commercialization drive growth.

sources.title: Native American campaign agenda
sources.evidence: Earlier dated position: tribal sovereignty, government-to-government relations, tribal environmental regulation, native-language early education, federal funding partnerships.

sources.title: CNN town hall transcript
sources.evidence: Would welcome state death-penalty abolition but retain very limited federal terrorism cases; reform incarceration and regulate fracking.

sources.title: CNN transcript: counterterror speech
sources.evidence: Intelligence surge and analysis of ISIS networks; encryption has security benefits and investigatory costs, favors commission and cooperation to protect safety and privacy.

sources.title: Reuters: Clinton criticizes Trump Fed comments
sources.evidence: Search-index excerpt: Fed monetary-policy comments should be off limits for presidents/candidates. Full page fetch rate-limited; narrower indexed evidence only.

sources.title: Council on Foreign Relations remarks
sources.evidence: Proposed northern Syrian no-fly zone, protected refuges and special forces against ISIS; regional autonomy within a reconstructed Syrian state.

sources.title: Washington Post: Clinton on press ban
sources.evidence: Later public check: she condemned White House restrictions on news outlets.

sources.title: Hard Choices official publisher page
sources.evidence: Publisher credits Hillary Rodham Clinton; political memoir of her secretary-of-state tenure. Publication date June 10, 2014.

sources.title: ÉPOCA: Brazilian release and foreign-policy excerpts
sources.evidence: Brazilian edition named Escolhas difíceis, Globo Livros, 766 pages; discusses intervention doctrine with excerpts.

sources.title: Sebo do Messias Brazilian edition listing
sources.evidence: Credits Hillary Rodham Clinton, Globo, 2016, ISBN 9788525060341, Brazilian title Escolhas Difíceis.

facts: 2016: local policing and state marijuana experiments survive national civil-rights guidelines.
2007: recognizes tribal sovereignty and native-language schools; 2016 health program incentivizes state Medicaid expansion.
estrutura.tension: Cooperative federalism with national rights floors, not either secession or a unitary police/education system.

facts: 2016: automatic registration and equal voting access.
2026-09-23: condemns media exclusion.
representacao.tension: Institutional representative democracy and constitutional protections, not rule by plebiscite or leader decree.

facts: 2016: reduce nonviolent incarceration, protect due process and police accountability.
2016: retain narrow federal capital punishment; intelligence surge and encryption compromise.
poder.tension: Civil-rights liberalism coexists with security powers and restrictive gun policy; not libertarian abolition of criminal law.

facts: 2016: citizenship pathway, asylum hearings, family unity, cultural integration.
2016: English education and deportation of violent threats remain.
imigracao.tension: Pluralism and lawful borders; neither forced cultural assimilation nor unrestricted entry.

facts: 2016: NATO and military capacity with diplomacy, Iran agreement and New START.
2015: Syrian no-fly zone and special forces.
diplomacia.tension: Hawkish liberal internationalism, not pacifism, but deterrence is not an exclusive theory of peace.

facts: 2016: sanctions, military alliances and counterterrorism outside US borders.
2015: Syrian no-fly zone and safe areas.
intervencao.tension: International institutions and allied cooperation are tools for active US leadership, not neutrality or isolation.

facts: 2016: ACA mixed-insurance system plus public option, Medicaid and community clinics.
2016: end private prisons; industrial partnerships with businesses.
economia.tension: Regulated private enterprise with public obligations, not worker ownership or wholesale privatization.

facts: 2016: financial risk fees, Volcker-rule strengthening, regulation and industrial incentives.
2016-09-06: defends Fed monetary-policy independence.
controle.tension: Government steering and redistribution without comprehensive command planning or political control of all monetary policy.

facts: 2016: rejects concluded TPP, backs Buy American and trade enforcement.
2016: technology exports and global-market competition remain desired.
comercio.tension: Selective worker/strategic protection inside international integration, not autarky or unconditional tariff abolition.

facts: 2016-01-25: describes Methodist faith and Christian charity as political motivations.
2016: marriage, transgender and reproductive rights independent of religious doctrine.
religiao.tension: Personal faith and religious pluralism alongside secular equal-rights law; neither theocracy nor anti-religious secularism.

facts: 2016: LGBT equality including adoption and gender identity; legal abortion.
2016: anti-trafficking remains part of foreign-policy record.
moral.tension: Equal-rights progressivism does not demonstrate endorsement of every sexual practice or commercial sex; 1990s/2000s marriage positions are not substituted for 2016.

facts: 2016: science funding, digital infrastructure, innovation and space exploration.
2016: conservation, oil-use reduction, pollution standards and clean-energy manufacturing.
tecnologia.tension: Technology with environmental and privacy safeguards; no demonstrated unrestricted transhumanist program.

limitations: Research checked through 2026-10-01; later press-freedom statement corroborates institutional commitments, not a comprehensive new campaign platform.
Campaign pages are primary advocacy sources, checked against CNN transcripts, TIME reporting, ACS candidate questionnaire, Reuters indexed reporting and Washington Post reporting.
Brazil-specific questions are interpreted through analogous US institutional principles; not claims Clinton endorsed Brazilian legislation.

Brain implants, embryo enhancement, cultivated meat, euthanasia and polyamory have sparse direct evidence. Answers must be labelled principled inferences; N only where competing commitments genuinely balance.
Earlier 2007 tribal agenda is dated explicitly; 2016 federalism is independently supported by state marijuana experiments and state Medicaid policy.
Reuters Fed page fetch failed with 429; only retrieved search excerpt supports that narrow finding.

recommendedMetadata.reason: Current PT/EN role, name and compact description remain accurate for the preserved campaign-era profile. Coordinator notified before any answers.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political/diplomatic memoir directly relevant to her foreign-policy doctrine. Existing books catalogue contains no entry for this personality. Publisher credits Hillary Rodham Clinton; Brazilian title verified against Globo-associated coverage and Brazilian edition listing. Selected for political relevance, not an unsupported claim of highest sales.

processNotes: Independent single-profile review. No existing answers, profile vectors or score reports read.
Read CONTRIBUTING.md, NEW_PROFILE.md, new-personality skill and README. No delegation.

Likely neighbours: Obama/Biden share institutional liberalism but Clinton advocated a Syria no-fly zone; Sanders differs on insurance system and force; Merkel differs on 2016 trade opposition and reproductive rights. These distinctions are factual, not numerical targets.
Research and metadata review completed before answers. Dedicated checks covered federalism, religion, security-versus-liberty, central-bank independence, technology and current remarks.
Each answer chosen in the unchanged template display order, then mapped to question ID. No numerical vector target was chosen.

Neutral choices express mixed commitments: national curriculum/local control; autonomy/end-of-life safeguards; partial decriminalization; cultural integration; multilateralism/power; mixed health provision and welfare design; distributional tax choices; personal faith/secular governance; family autonomy/child rights; research/environment and therapeutic/enhancement tradeoffs.

Sparse-evidence affirmative/disagree responses on implants, cultivated meat, spatial lifestyle and Brazilian policy analogies are reasoned extrapolations from documented scientific, environmental and institutional commitments, not reported explicit endorsements.

Original validator blocks merge for similarity to Kamala Harris and Mark Carney. No answers modified after viewing validation; no score tuning, no exception and no merge. Coordinator must resolve the explicit duplicate-profile consent requirement with the user.
